title: Multi-Agent Escalation Policy
evidenceBase: EVAL-8: Multi-agent benefits not yet proven. Escalation should be conditional, not default.

escalationTiers.name: Factory Lite Core (Default)
escalationTiers.model: No role model. Manual Router + POR only.

escalationTiers.name: 3-Role Model (Optional)
escalationTiers.trigger: Projects meeting ANY: (a) >10 FRs with auth/RBAC, (b) separate frontend+backend, (c) user explicitly requests review

escalationTiers.name: Full Multi-Agent (Experimental)
escalationTiers.trigger: Projects meeting ALL: (a) >20 FRs, (b) separate teams/agents for frontend/backend, (c) dedicated QA infrastructure, (d) user explicitly requests multi-agent
escalationTiers.model: Architect + Frontend + Backend + Database + Integrator + QA + Security + Verifier + Auditor + PM
escalationTiers.warning: EVAL-8 showed 10-role model underperforms Factory Lite for moderate projects. Use only when complexity genuinely requires role separation.

escalationRules: Default: Tier 0 (Factory Lite Core) — no role model
User may request Tier 1 (3-role) for any project
Tier 1 automatically suggested when project has auth/RBAC + separate frontend/backend
Tier 2 requires explicit user confirmation AND multi-agent infrastructure
Never auto-escalate from Tier 0 to Tier 2
If Tier 2 underperforms, fall back to Tier 1 or Tier 0
antiPatterns: Using 10-role model for a single-developer project
Creating cross-role contracts when only one agent builds everything
Adding process artifacts to compensate for missing product quality
